text: Succeeding or failing with a value is fine. But what if we want to do something more computery? Effect.sync takes a function of no arguments, a.k.a. a thunk, and stores it in an Effect. Here we'll log a message and return new Date(). By the way, Effect's laziness isn't magic. It's inherited from the functions it wraps. When we run it, the thunk will be called, our message will be logged, and we'll succeed with a Date. If we run it again, the thunk will be called again, and we'll get a new Date.
